author: charly26
text_post: Was it ok to set this boundary? HI: My younger 19-year-old gf has been looking for a job,and now she has been called by pizza hut to work there. This is gonna be her first work experience. When she presented her documents with other girl, the manager made this statement: "who's got a bf? because once you start working here, you'll break up with your bfs since the guys here are such players" I told her that i hope that that statement won't happen with her, and she was like, of course not, I'm only interested in you. Then I told her I don't want her to go to wild drinking parties with the people from work because once there and with beers many things can happen and I will not tolerate any kind of cheating from her, if that happens, it's totally over. She said that of course she doesn't plan to go to those wild parties where they drink a lot, maybe just go out to a mall and do something more relaxing to which I said it was ok. She said she doesn't want to lose me because she's in love with me, but in some ways i was afraid that she could meet players and guys who know how to make women cheat on the boyfriends. I think setting this boundary was ok..  would you have done the same? if not, what would you have done or said instead?

author: TheRogue
text_post: Obviously the manager made that statement as a joke. I would have just laughed it off and not taken it seriously. So what if she meets "players?" It's still her choice whether to cheat or not, and if your relationship and her moral values are strong, cheating should not even be in question. Rogue

author: Fact0r

If she's really "in love" and knows she's dating a non-insecure (work on this) and a solid dude she won't cheat.  However, if you keep telling her she can't go to those parties and she finds out they are a blast (beer pong/bonfires/dancing/etc.) she'll go regardless of what you tell her. Chicks like confident dudes, and if you show off as otherwise, this relationship won't last long, trust me I've been there.

author: deepseadiver
text_post: I wouldn't mention it.  If she brings it up, just apologize for overreacting and make fun of the situation to lighten things up a bit. This is not a 'boundary' per se on your part, but rather an attempt to control an imagined future possibility.  It's a projection of your fears and your insecurities.  She has not violated her relationship rights in any way.   I would drop it, and learn from the mistake.  You don't want her walking on eggshells around you, because then she is not the human being she was born to be.

author: missmiami
text_post: I've tried responding to this, like I did for Hoplessly's post below about him being 42 and his gf being 25. I've written and erased this like 12 times, and I've tried as best I could not to make it a personal attack; but here it is.  I'm 27, and I lead a boring life. Since I was 19, I've dropped out of 3 colleges, moved out, changed employers 3 times, moved across the country twice, rented 4 apartments, thought about buying a house, bought 3 cars, got engaged, got un-engaged, had this many boyfriends, slept with that many people, and had a couple flings.  What the hell do I have in common with a 19 year old working at Pizza Hut? Not a fucking thing. Unless you stopped growing emotionally, socially, financially, and professionally; you having nothing in common with her either - she is not on your level. There are major benchmarks in your life, moving out, going to school, getting a job, getting a house, getting married, getting babies, and things like that there. She is nineTEEN, she is a teenager, unless you live at home with your mom, play video games and work at Burger King; you should not be with her.  So let me tell you some of what me and all of my friends think about situations such as this.  1. We think nobody your age or level wants to deal with your shit. That no girl in your age range, in your tax bracket, field of work, or any regular girl wants to deal with your shit. Nobody wants you, you are the shit left over. So by default you must get with significantly younger chicks, who don't know any better. 2. You have what I refer to as the "Nurse/Flight Attendant" complex. Instead of a doctor, you choose nurse, a legal secretary over an attorney, and a flight attendant over a pilot. You want someone less than, not equal to.  3. You never matured past 19.  Regardless, it is not a good look.  I work with a girl, 37 - divorced, no kids, she began dating a guy 56 - twice divorced and has 2 grown kids, 24 and 28. Nobody understood it; she was looking to make babies, and he was looking to be a grandpa. Another girl I worked with was 25, dating some dude who was 48; again nobody got it, and all we did was talk shit. There's not a difference if you are 38, divorced with 2 kids, and he's 46 with kids the same age. Or if you're 28 and he's 36 - and you both have never had kids or been married. There is  HUGE difference between 19 and 31. I know it sounds harsh and I sound bitter, but I'm really not. I'm actually quite charming in real life, you'll just have to take my word for it.
